title: Infernal Tactics (Alpha 2.0): Claude (coding) + 19th-century engravings (sprites and cards) + Codex (backgrounds, UI, and some coding). Built with Godot.
author: One_Code_Wonders
selftext:
[https://one-code-wonders.itch.io/infernal-tactics](https://one-code-wonders.itch.io/infernal-tactics)

Infernal Tactics is a tactical roguelike deckbuilder combining army building, positional combat and demonic bargains.

I've just completed a major gameplay and graphical overhaul following feedback on the original alpha. The game now features shared movement points, defensive formations, five playable Houses and infernal bargains with lasting consequences.

I'm particularly interested in any advice on how I could use AI to improve my game (whether in terms of presentation or gameplay). Do you guys think I should try to do animations? AI seems able to generate pretty accurate sprites (really close to originals) with the right prompts. Or do you guys think the current 'paper units' style is best left alone? 

Honest feedback on looks or gameplay is welcome (no matter how harsh). Thank you!
